title: Understanding patient experiences of starting to use non-invasive ventilation (NIV)
official: Exploring patient ventilation journeys: from hospital to home
summary:
Background and study aims
Respiratory disease affects one in five people in England, many of whom experience breathing difficulties and require some kind of medical assistance. If someone has a condition where the muscles in their chest wall are weakened (e.g. muscular dystrophy) or the lungs themselves are damaged (e.g. COPD), a device such as a Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure machine (BiPAP) can help. A BiPAP is a small, portable ventilator which pushes air into and out of the lungs via a mask which is placed over a person’s nose and mouth. Because it does not require surgery or placing something inside the body, this treatment is considered a non-invasive form of ventilation (NIV). Despite benefits such as reduced tiredness and more stable regulation of harmful carbon dioxide levels in the body, previous research shows that there are barriers to using NIV and that some people find it difficult to get used to. This can impact how frequently they use the machine and how effectively it can help to improve their breathing. Our study will explore what some of these barriers are in detail by seeking to understand the lived experience of starting NIV from the patient’s perspective. It aims to examine the day-to-day realities of adjusting to NIV, considering how this is experienced by patients and their families over time. The goal is to use what we learn from this research to work alongside patients and clinicians in the NHS to improve support for NIV users by placing patients’ voices and their everyday  experiences at the centre of provision around NIV.  

Who can participate?
1.	Clinicians over the age of 18 years who work at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals in a role that involves regular contact with patients who use non-invasive ventilation (NIV) or whose work is related to the set-up, maintenance or management of NIV services or machines
2.	Patients over the age of 18 years who at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals who are about to start or have very recently started using NIV
3.	Relatives and other important people to patients who are taking part in the research can also take part if they are over the age of 18 years 

What does the study involve?
There are four different parts to the study.
1.	Clinicians will be invited to take part in an interview to talk about their experiences of NIV and supporting patients
2.	Patients who are starting NIV will take part in a case study for four months so we can learn about their experiences over time. They will take part in three interviews and complete a weekly diary or scrapbook. They may also invite the researcher to observe any clinic appointments or home visits where their NIV treatment is discussed
3.	A small number of patients who are admitted to hospital in Sheffield to be supported to start on NIV can consent for their treatment to be observed over a few days
4.	Patients who are offered NIV but decide not to start using it can take part in an interview to talk about how they made this decision and why

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There will be no immediate benefits to those taking part in the study. But there may be benefits for patients who start non-invasive ventilation in the future. This is because the research will be used to inform ventilation services in the NHS and to improve patient experience. The main risk for people taking part is that this research may involve talking about sensitive and personal experiences which could be upsetting. All participants will be informed at the start of the research that they can stop taking part at any time and they will be provided with information about a range of support organisations. 

Where is the study run from?
The study is being run by the University of Sheffield and takes place at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals. 

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
November 2026 to December 2028

Who is funding the study?
Wellcome Trust (UK) [226472/Z/22/Z]

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
To be included in the study health care staff must:
1. Be employees of Sheffield Teaching Hospitals
2. Be aged 18 years or over
3. Have capacity to provide informed consent 
4. Be employed in a role which involves regular contact with patients who use NIV or  is related to the set-up, maintenance or management of NIV services or technologies 

To be included in the study patients must: 
1. Be a patient at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals
2. Be aged 18 years or over
3. Be about to start using or have very recently either started using NIV or declined to start using it (i.e. in the last 2 months)
4. Be aware of their treatment plan 
5. Have capacity to provide informed consent to take part 

To take part in the study relatives or significant others must:
1. Be aged 18 years or over
2. Be identified by the patient as playing an important part in their everyday life 
3. Have capacity to provide informed consent to take part
Exclusion criteria:
Health care staff:
1. Not being employed by Sheffield Teaching Hospitals
2. Role does not involve NIV
3. Under 18 years of age 
4. Unable to provide informed consent

Patients: 
1. Under 18 years of age
2. Unable to provide informed consent
3. Not been offered NIV (including patients who use other types of breathing support)
4. Been using NIV for more than 2 months 

Relatives or significant others:
1. Under 18 years of age 
2. Unable to provide informed consent
3. Patient they have a relationship with does not want to take part in the study
4. Patient they have a relationship with does not want them to take part in the study
